name: Money Smart: Financial Literacy for Everyone
description: For everyone: budgeting, saving, interest, and scam awareness - practical money skills for students, families, and young professionals.

options: A plan for how you spend and save money
questions.explanation: A budget is a plan that tracks income and spending.

questions.prompt: What does "save first" or pay yourself first mean?
questions.explanation: Paying yourself first builds savings before expenses tempt you.

questions.prompt: If you save 100 pesos a week, how much in 10 weeks (no interest)?
What is interest on a savings account?
options: Money the bank pays you for keeping deposits
questions.explanation: Banks pay interest as a reward for using your deposits.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a "need" rather than a "want"?
questions.explanation: Basic food is a need; the rest are wants.

questions.prompt: What is an emergency fund for?
options: Unexpected expenses like illness or repairs
questions.explanation: An emergency fund covers surprises without going into debt.

questions.prompt: A loan charges 5% interest on 10,000 pesos for one year. How much interest?
Which is the safest reaction to a text saying you won a prize and must send a fee?
options: Ignore and report it - likely a scam
questions.explanation: Legitimate prizes never ask for fees or PINs - it is a scam pattern.

questions.prompt: What does diversification mean in investing?
options: Putting all money in one stock
questions.explanation: Diversification spreads risk across different assets.

questions.prompt: Which habit best helps avoid debt?
questions.explanation: Spending less than you earn is the core of avoiding debt.
Inflation means money buys less as prices rise over time.

questions.prompt: How long should an emergency fund ideally cover?
questions.explanation: Experts suggest 3-6 months of essential expenses.
Rent stays the same each month, so it is a fixed expense.

questions.prompt: What should you check before borrowing money?
options: Total cost, interest, and your ability to repay
questions.explanation: Always check the total repayment cost and affordability.

questions.prompt: Tracking every expense for a month helps you to...
options: See where your money actually goes
questions.explanation: Tracking reveals spending leaks you can fix.
